method: FFmpeg-decoded original videos: left-camera overviews sampled every second, plus selected stereo frames spaced 0.5–1 s apart around contact, release and pull-through; images directly visually inspected. No simulation or replay overlay was substituted.
timebase: Encoded MP4 PTS in seconds from clip start; frame indices are zero-based at 30 FPS. These are not a new robot-camera time calibration.
contact_sheet_label_note: Detail-sheet frame labels are selected-image ordinals, not source frame indices; PTS labels and selected_frames.json identify source frames.
source_hash_note: All reviewed original video files were independently SHA-256 checked on 2026-11-10; every digest matches the retained prepared provenance.

observations.visible_feature: The grasped needle moves above the incision; no pronounced local lip notch is visible.
A local notch develops at the upper lip and the bright needle tip becomes visible in the incision opening.
The needle advances across the opening and through the lower lip. Both lip contours deform locally; the lower exposed metal segment lengthens.
The tool releases and moves to regrasp. The lip contours largely relax while separated visible needle segments remain on either side of tissue and across the opening.
Pulling the exposed needle produces another local V-shaped distortion, followed by lip relaxation as the metal slides through and the thread follows.
Needle repositioning and approach occur above a comparatively smooth incision lip.
A shallow local depression becomes a clear V-shaped upper-lip notch as the needle advances.
Both incision lips undergo pronounced local displacement around the needle. This is present in both stereo views; portions of the needle remain occluded by tissue.
The tool opens/releases and repositions. The lips largely relax while the needle remains visibly spanning the incision, with exposed metal above, within the opening, and below the tissue.
Regrasping and pulling the lower exposed segment creates another strong local V-shaped lip deformation.
The metal slides out and the thread follows; the lip contours relax despite continued tool/needle motion.
The grasped needle lifts/repositions away from the lip without a comparable local notch developing.
The initially smooth upper-lip contour develops a localized notch, clearly visible at 3.7–4.0 s.
The needle advances across the incision opening and through the opposite lip; both lips develop a pronounced local V-shaped deformation.
The gripper opens/repositions and the lips relax while the needle still visibly spans the tissue and opening.
Pulling the lower exposed needle recreates localized lip tenting/distortion in both stereo views.
Metal slides through, thread follows, and the lip contours relax.
Two tools grasp, transfer and reorient the free curved needle. The visible incision retains a broadly smooth contour without the large localized V deformation seen during the subsequent throw.

model_comparison_priorities: Separate pre-entry surface indentation, embedded-shaft transverse bearing, tangential sliding, tool release and final shaft disengagement.
An outside tip does not establish that the shaft is disengaged: the clips show metal on both sides of tissue while lips respond to handling.
Include release/relaxation and regrasp/pull-through cases; one smooth prescribed insertion arc does not cover all observed handling.
Retain separated incision lips and the intervening empty space; do not replace the visible gap with solid material.
Audit material-anchor retention, engaged track length, transverse needle/anchor separation and finite-shaft endpoint coverage before attributing weak deformation solely to stiffness.
safe_comparison_metrics: Order and source-frame brackets of visible indentation, appearance in the gap, opposite-lip emergence, release, regrasp and relaxation.
Projected lip-contour displacement relative to nearby far-field pad landmarks, in pixels and separately in each camera; register camera/pad motion first.
Local notch depth relative to a line through its two neighboring lip points, normalized by visible local lip width; avoid occluded contour intervals.
Projected material motion versus projected needle motion during loaded and sliding intervals, with explicit visibility masks.
Relaxation interval after release or disengagement, with frame-bracket uncertainty.
limitations: These selected frames establish visible behavior, not exact puncture times, hidden shaft contact, measured forces, material modulus, friction coefficients or world-Z displacement.
No new metric stereo calibration, segmentation, 3D reconstruction or numerical displacement estimate was performed.
Thread and gripper can also transmit loads in the footage; the current needle-only example omits those mechanisms.
Session name tissue_3 does not identify FEM region 3; prepared workbench provenance associates these source recordings with wound 1.
No 60 FPS or physical-calibration claim follows from this review.
